study_window.reason: The first administration under study begins 1999-05-29 (Obasanjo). Data before that describes a different exchange-rate and fiscal regime and cannot inform any estimate this project makes.
study_window.outside_window: Data outside the window is still landed and still gated for provenance, but it is not gated for gaps or spikes: it is retained for pre-trend inspection and for the synthetic-control pre-treatment fit, not analysed as an outcome.

adjudicated.reason: Brent for the month averaged $18.38 in April 2020 and $29.38 in May — the COVID-19 demand collapse and its first rebound. The largest in-window move in the series and entirely real.

breaks.label: WTI negative-price episode
breaks.note: Brent is quoted here, not WTI, so no negative print reaches this series. The annotation is carried because the two benchmarks are routinely conflated when the 2020 window is discussed.

breaks.label: GDP rebasing
breaks.note: Nigeria rebased GDP to a 2010 base year, roughly doubling measured nominal GDP and shifting the level of the series. Level comparisons across April 2014 are not meaningful.

adjudicated.reason: The January 2025 CPI rebasing; see `definition_breaks` for cpi_yoy.

breaks.label: CPI rebasing (2024 base year)
breaks.note: The NBS rebased the Consumer Price Index in January 2025 — the first rebasing since 2009 — on a new 2024 base year with an updated basket. Headline inflation fell from 34.80% in December 2024 to 24.48% in January 2025, largely because of the rebasing rather than a change in prices (Reuters, 2025-02-18; NBS release). The World Bank's annual averages inherit this: 33.24% for 2024 against 23.01% for 2025. Comparison across January 2025 mixes disinflation with a measurement change and must be annotated, not smoothed.

breaks.label: Labour-force methodology change
breaks.note: NBS moved to the ILO-aligned definition, lifting measured unemployment substantially. The series is not comparable across this date.

breaks.label: Methodology revision
breaks.note: NBS revised the definition again; the level steps down.

adjudicated.reason: The 2023-06-14 FX unification; the official rate steps as multiple windows collapse.
The second leg of the same unification: the annual average for 2024 (+129%) reflects a full year at the unified rate against a 2023 average that was mostly pegged.

breaks.label: Naira floated
breaks.note: The CBN abandoned the pegged rate for a managed float. The official rate series steps, and the premium over the parallel rate narrows sharply. A single official series understates the effective rate before this date.

breaks.label: FX unification
breaks.note: Multiple official windows were collapsed into a single rate, producing an immediate large step. Classified as a definitional break rather than a data error, which is why it is annotated here and not merely flagged by the spike gate.

adjudicated.reason: Net ODA to Nigeria rose 1006% in one year ($0.58bn -> $6.4bn) because Paris Club debt relief is recorded as ODA. The OECD attributes the 2005 global ODA peak to "large Paris Club debt relief operations (notably for Iraq and Nigeria)"; UNCTAD records the same. Nigeria's US$18bn deal was announced October 2005 and completed April 2006.
Second year of the same debt-relief entry, on the flow basis the series uses.
The -82.9% reversal is the same artefact unwinding: with the relief booked in 2005-06, the 2007 flow returns to the underlying level.
